distinguishing_features: Passive dielectric permittivity grading via a low-ε porous pad placed at high-field barrier interfaces to reduce local E-field below PD inception
Relies on static material permittivity contrast (capacitive divider) to reshape the field during fast-rising voltage spikes, not on monitoring or chemical dosing
No active instrumentation, chemistry, or control-loop; mitigation is a physical material property modification within the existing insulation casting
Addresses transient-driven partial discharge inception locally at defect hotspots rather than detection/alerting or corrosion electrochemistry
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to locally reduce peak electric field intensity at insulation defect hotspots during fast-rising voltage transients below the partial-discharge inception threshold, without thickening the bulk insulation or adding active monitoring.
parsed.viable_reason: Inserting a low-permittivity porous pad at a high-field interface is a physically grounded capacitive-field-grading approach feasible within existing casting processes, though the stated 40% field reduction should be verified since permittivity grading at interfaces is geometry-dependent and the simple ratio $R=\epsilon_{ins}/\epsilon_{eff}$ is a simplification.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art teaches permittivity-based field grading during voltage transients; the existing art is limited to monitoring/inference or chemical depassivation, so physically inserting a low-ε voided pad to reshape local fields at spike conditions is not an obvious step from that prior art.
